Ultimately and eternally empty;

one analyzes and seeks the source until reaching the division of a single hair.

Following the conventions of ordinary people, one speaks of the name "minute particle," but it is not said that it has a fixed characteristic;

If he speaks of non-self...

yet if one speaks of emptiness, then nothing exists at all.

Because the five views are each distinct.

as causes, transform into effects.

seeking the ultimate principle down to the subtlest atom.

there is nothing to be extinguished;
just as I am fundamentally non-existent from the beginning.
Although one speaks of non-existence,
one does not fall into the view of nihilism;
thus, by means of the gate of selflessness.

one does not fall into annihilation;
furthermore, this is the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Although it is said that form and so forth are empty down to the level of atoms,
this also applies to the mind and mental factors.

yet does not fall into cessation. Why is this?
It is taught solely for the purpose of destroying inverted and false views;
it is not the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena.
If one speaks of impermanence...

where there is an effect, there must be a cause.

for coarse objects consist of many aggregations.

thus it is whether the form be coarse or subtle.
Whether far or near,
whether beautiful or ugly,
whether past or future.
All are entirely false and illusory,

It is only intended to cause people's minds to give rise to weary detachment and thereby attain nirvana; feeling,

Seeing that there are faults and afflictions [in existence],

the Buddha’s intention was to cause beings to transcend both existence and non-existence.

furthermore, there is no dharma whatsoever.
Those who do not understand the Buddha’s intention [will be confused].

When these are removed, there is no interval;
yet when one seeks mutual penetration and benefit, there is obstruction. Why is this?
Because the preceding mind is not the subsequent mind,
minds do not know one another;
the preceding thought-moment is not the subsequent thought-moment.
Although they are identical, they function as two;
thus, the scriptural statement regarding the recollection of past lives and the doctrine that later consciousness cognizes prior consciousness have their meaning made clear.

this subsequent visual consciousness functions with sharpness and possesses power."

by inferring from this, one may speak further.
Then a subsequent thought could recollect a preceding consciousness.

the dull-witted should likewise do so.

When this mindfulness arises, it...

The suchness of the past and present is the suchness of the future.

as the Buddha told the bhikṣus,
